claim_verdicts.claim_text: The chart documents a penicillin allergy that is severe, with anaphylaxis to amoxicillin in 2019 that required epinephrine.

citations.quote: Entry 1 | Allergen: penicillins (reaction occurred with amoxicillin) | Type: allergy | Severity: severe
Entry 1 | Reaction: anaphylaxis (generalized hives, throat tightness, hypotension) | Onset: 2019-05 | Treated in an emergency department with intramuscular epinephrine

claim_verdicts.why: The allergy list entry records a severe penicillin allergy with the reaction occurring with amoxicillin, and the reaction entry records anaphylaxis from 2019-05 treated with intramuscular epinephrine. The claim accurately reports what the chart documents.
claim_verdicts.uncertainty: The answer cites a triage note (N006) reporting NKDA that is not among the shown lines, so the chart's current status is not fully settled, though this does not contradict what the cited allergy entry documents.

claim_verdicts.claim_text: The penicillin allergy is corroborated by the 2024 clinic note.

citations.quote: Allergies reviewed with patient: in May 2019 amoxicillin caused hives, throat swelling and low blood pressure that required epinephrine in the emergency department.

claim_verdicts.why: The 2024-08-12 clinic note (C005) records the amoxicillin reaction in 2019 with hives, throat swelling and low blood pressure requiring epinephrine, which is the penicillin-class allergy history the claim says it corroborates. The note documents the history as reviewed with the patient, not as newly tested.
claim_verdicts.uncertainty: The note reports patient history only; no allergy testing or challenge was performed (C006), so the allergy is documented by history rather than objectively confirmed. The 2026 triage note records NKDA (N006), which is a separate conflict not addressed by this claim.

claim_verdicts.claim_text: The 2026-02-14 triage note says the patient has no known drug allergies (NKDA), which conflicts with the documented penicillin allergy.
claim_verdicts.why: Line N006 in the 2026-02-14 ED triage note records NKDA, which is what the claim reports. The claim also says this conflicts with the documented penicillin allergy, which is shown in A004 and A005 but not cited here.
claim_verdicts.uncertainty: The record does not show which entry is correct, and nothing documents re-evaluation after the triage entry.
